tasks.gr10-vectors-motion-mechanical-energy-t3: Grade 10 Physical Sciences Term 3: Vectors, kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, and mechanical energy.
tasks.gr10-chemical-change-stoichiometry-t3: Grade 10 Physical Sciences Term 3: Reactions in aqueous solution, quantitative aspects of chemical change.
tasks.gr10-ions-in-solution-t3: Topic: Ions in aqueous solution. Cover how water molecules (polar, with partial charges) surround the ions of an ionic solid and pull them apart, dissolution equations with state symbols such as NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), CaCl₂(s) → Ca²⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq), that the charges balance, that ions in solution carry current so conductivity depends on the concentration of ions, and ion concentration from the formula (for example 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ CaCl₂ gives 0,1 of Ca²⁺ and 0,2 of Cl⁻). Ask Grade 10 learners to write dissolution equations and to compare the ion concentrations of solutions.
tasks.gr10-precipitation-reaction-types-t3: Topic: Precipitation and reaction types in aqueous solution. Cover ion exchange, solubility rules (all nitrates and salts of Group 1 and ammonium soluble; chlorides, bromides and iodides soluble except silver and lead; sulfates soluble except barium and lead; carbonates and hydroxides insoluble except Group 1 and ammonium), a precipitate written (s), tests for anions with silver nitrate and barium nitrate and nitric acid, and the four reaction types with their driving forces: precipitation, gas formation, acid-base (protons) and redox (electrons, shown by the change of charge, for example Zn from 0 to +2). Ask Grade 10 learners to predict precipitates, identify reaction types and identify anions from observations.
tasks.gr10-composition-empirical-formula-t3: Topic: Percentage composition and empirical formulae. Cover molar mass from relative atomic masses (quote Ar in the question: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, Mg = 24, S = 32, Cl = 35,5, K = 39, Ca = 40, Fe = 56, Cu = 63,5, Al = 27), n = m/M, the percentage of an element in a compound, the empirical formula from percentage or mass composition (moles, divide by the smallest, whole numbers), and the water of crystallisation in a hydrated salt (moles of water per mole of salt). Ask Grade 10 learners to calculate with these.
tasks.gr10-concentration-gas-yield-t3: Topic: Concentration, molar volume and theoretical yield. Cover c = n/V in mol·dm⁻³ with V in dm³ (cm³ divided by 1 000), preparing a solution (n = cV, m = nM), the molar volume of a gas 22,4 dm³·mol⁻¹ at 273 K and 101,3 kPa (quote it in each question that needs it), and the theoretical yield of a product from a known mass of reactant using the mole ratio of a balanced equation (quote the Ar values). Ask Grade 10 learners to calculate concentration, mass, gas volume and yield.
